summary_paragraph: A 54-year-old woman with a complex medical history including Crohn’s disease, multiple prior abdominal surgeries, and a history of paralytic ileus presented with abdominal distention, vomiting, and right flank pain. Imaging revealed colonic ileus without obstruction, likely exacerbated by recent opioid use for presumed nephrolithiasis. She was managed conservatively with NG tube decompression, NPO status, IV fluids, and pain control. A urinary tract infection caused by ciprofloxacin-resistant E. coli was identified, and antibiotics were adjusted to nitrofurantoin. Her bowel function gradually improved, allowing NG tube removal and advancement to a regular diet. She remained stable, with resolution of tachycardia and no signs of systemic infection. Blood cultures remained negative. She was discharged home with a plan to complete antibiotics, manage pain and nausea as needed, and follow up with her primary and gastroenterology providers.
